params.question: A patient with heart failure wakes up gasping for breath 90 minutes after falling asleep. Which category of heart failure symptoms does this episode represent?

answers.text: Forward failure due to reduced cardiac output

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Forward failure causes fatigue, nocturia, and eventually weight loss — all from inadequate tissue perfusion. Waking up breathless reflects fluid backing up into the lungs, not low output.
Right-sided backward failure raises systemic venous pressure, producing ankle oedema, hepatomegaly, and raised JVP. Respiratory symptoms from pulmonary congestion point to the left side.

Correct. Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea occurs when recumbency redistributes fluid from the periphery into the pulmonary circulation, raising capillary pressure enough to cause alveolar oedema — a classic left-sided backward failure symptom.
Biventricular failure is common in advanced disease, but this symptom specifically reflects raised pulmonary capillary pressure from left-sided congestion, not a forward-output problem.

overallFeedback.feedback: PND belongs to left-sided backward failure. Lying flat redistributes peripheral fluid into the pulmonary circulation, raising capillary pressure and causing breathlessness — not a right-sided or forward failure pattern.
Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea is a hallmark of left-sided backward failure — fluid shifts into the lungs during recumbency, raising pulmonary capillary pressure.

interactions.label: The most common cause of right heart failure in clinical practice is cor pulmona

params.question: The most common cause of right heart failure in clinical practice is cor pulmonale due to chronic lung disease.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Cor pulmonale is the most important cause of isolated right heart failure, but in everyday practice the most common cause of right heart failure is actually left heart failure. Back-pressure from the left side eventually overloads the right ventricle, which is why biventricular failure is what you see most often.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Cor pulmonale is the most important cause of isolated right heart failure, but the most common cause of right heart failure overall is left heart failure — left-sided congestion eventually overloads the right ventricle, producing combined biventricular failure.

interactions.label: A patient with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 28% has a widened QRS c

params.question: A patient with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 28% has a widened QRS complex with broad, notched R waves in the lateral leads. What is the most important clinical implication of this finding?

answers.text: It confirms ischaemic heart disease as the underlying cause

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ischaemic aetiology is suggested by pathological Q waves indicating prior infarction, not by QRS widening. This pattern reflects a conduction abnormality in the His-Purkinje system.

answers.text: It indicates the need for urgent coronary angiography

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Coronary angiography is indicated when ischaemia is suspected. This QRS pattern is a conduction defect whose clinical importance lies in guiding device therapy, not revascularisation.

answers.text: It requires immediate anticoagulation guided by a CHA₂DS₂-VASc score

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CHA₂DS₂-VASc scoring guides anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation, which appears as an irregularly irregular rhythm without clear P waves — a different ECG pattern entirely.

answers.text: It identifies the patient as a candidate for cardiac resynchronisation therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Left bundle branch block with a widened QRS in a patient with reduced ejection fraction is the key trigger for considering cardiac resynchronisation therapy, which can improve both symptoms and survival.

overallFeedback.feedback: This pattern describes left bundle branch block. In a patient with reduced EF, LBBB is the key trigger for cardiac resynchronisation therapy — not anticoagulation (that is for AF) or angiography (that is for suspected ischaemia).
LBBB with reduced ejection fraction is the principal indication for cardiac resynchronisation therapy — one of the most important ECG-to-management links in heart failure.

interactions.label: Which of the following drugs used in heart failure management improves symptoms

params.question: Which of the following drugs used in heart failure management improves symptoms but does NOT reduce mortality?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ARNI is the first pillar of GDMT and has shown the strongest mortality reduction among RAAS blockers. It pairs an ARB with a neprilysin inhibitor and is disease-modifying, not merely symptomatic.

Correct. Digoxin improves symptoms and reduces heart failure hospitalisations, but it does not extend survival. It sits outside the four mortality-reducing pillars — an important distinction for clinical decision-making.
Spironolactone is a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (the third pillar of GDMT). It blocks aldosterone, reducing sodium retention and cardiac fibrosis, and has a proven mortality benefit.
SGLT2 inhibitors like dapagliflozin are the newest pillar of GDMT. They reduce cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalisation regardless of whether the patient has diabetes.

overallFeedback.feedback: The four pillars that reduce mortality are RAAS blockers (ACEi/ARB/ARNI), evidence-based beta-blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and SGLT2 inhibitors. Digoxin and diuretics help with symptoms only.

Digoxin and diuretics control symptoms but do not reduce mortality — a crucial distinction from the four GDMT pillars (RAAS blockers, beta-blockers, MRAs, SGLT2 inhibitors) that are truly disease-modifying.

params.question: A young adult has fixed splitting of the second heart sound on auscultation. There is no cyanosis or clubbing. Which congenital heart lesion is most likely?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: VSD produces a harsh pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border due to turbulent flow across the interventricular septum. Fixed splitting of S2 is not a feature of VSD.

Tetralogy of Fallot is a cyanotic lesion with right-to-left shunting, producing central cyanosis and clubbing. This patient has neither, and the boot-shaped heart on CXR — not fixed splitting — is the classic radiological sign.

Correct. Fixed splitting of the second heart sound is the hallmark of ASD. The persistent left-to-right shunt maintains constant right ventricular volume overload throughout the respiratory cycle, preventing the normal variation in A2–P2 splitting.
PDA produces a continuous 'machinery' murmur because the pressure gradient between aorta and pulmonary artery persists throughout systole and diastole. Fixed splitting of S2 points to ASD, not PDA.

overallFeedback.feedback: Fixed splitting of the second heart sound is the hallmark of atrial septal defect. The persistent left-to-right shunt maintains right ventricular volume overload throughout the respiratory cycle, unlike the dynamic splitting seen in normal hearts.
Fixed splitting of S2 is pathognomonic of ASD — the constant left-to-right shunt keeps right ventricular volume elevated regardless of respiration, preventing normal splitting variation.
